EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development is Iran's definitive rejection of a full Strait of Hormuz reopening without extensive US concessions, coupled with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's firm refusal of the Gaza peace plan and any IDF withdrawal. These stances escalate regional tensions significantly, while the US grapples with munitions shortages from the ongoing "Iran war" and a defense pact emerges between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, indicating a volatile and unpredictable environment.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran are ongoing, with US Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg ordering defense contractors to accelerate weapon production due to critical munitions shortages caused by the "Iran war." Six US KC-135 refueling aircraft were damaged in operations against Iran, five in a missile attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia and one in an aerial collision over Iraq, requiring major repairs in Oklahoma. Iran's Army Ground Force Commander, General Ali Jahanshahi, declared full combat readiness, warning to "cut off feet" of any invading troops. IRGC Spokesperson Brigadier General Mohebbi stated that Iran's strategy is to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until the US accepts all Iranian conditions.

Internally, President Masoud Pezeshkian met with Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei to discuss national challenges, the ongoing war, military developments, and economic engagement. Major General Mohsen Rezaei, a veteran IRGC commander, was appointed as the Leader's representative to the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) and subsequently as SNSC Secretary by President Pezeshkian. Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr was appointed as the Leader's political adviser. The internal political situation is marked by disagreements, with President Pezeshkian's faction reportedly concerned about economic collapse and favoring a deal with the US, while IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi's faction rejects concessions. The US assesses Iran faces severe economic hardship, high inflation, and a lack of funds to pay soldiers, exacerbated by the US naval blockade. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi affirmed no new negotiations with the US until violations of the "Islamabad MoU" are rectified and compensation for violations is made. He also clarified that ongoing talks with Oman only concern establishing new maritime routes through the Strait of Hormuz, not its immediate reopening, which depends on conditions conveyed via intermediaries.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included the 55th Brigade and Yahalom forces locating and destroying an underground pit used for Hezbollah weapon storage in southern Lebanon, seizing Kalashnikovs, anti-tank missiles/launchers, artillery, and RPGs. Artillery strikes were reported in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh governorate. IDF fire was reported in Al-Zahra, west of Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip. Four Israeli soldiers injured last week in southern Lebanon were being treated at Rambam Medical Center; one is stable and conscious, while three remain sedated and intubated. Loud explosions and tremors were reported by residents in Haifa and the Krayot area, attributed by Israeli media to "IDF activity in the area."

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu explicitly rejected the "Gaza Board of Peace 15-point plan," stating Israel would not withdraw until Hamas is genuinely disarmed (heavy, lighter, and small weapons). He further declared that no Palestinian state would be established while he is prime minister, asserting Israel's readiness to stand firm on its interests even against its closest allies. The Israeli government approved an allocation of 1 billion ILS for urgent, classified defense procurement for 2026. The Commander of Central Command signed an intention to confiscate and demolish the home of Duaas Hassoun, who carried out the March 21, 2026 attack in Beit Amrin, which killed Yehuda Sherman. The US requested Israel end conflicts on three active fronts, but Israel informed American officials that it reserves the right for independent action against Iran if there are signs of continued nuclear weapon development or ballistic missile rebuilding.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli military forces conducted ground operations with reported firing in Al-Zahra, west of Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip. The humanitarian situation is highlighted by a flotilla preparing to sail for Gaza to break the Israeli siege and a Palestinian prisoners’ advocacy group reporting intensified torture and "slow killing" of Palestinian inmates due to an extended ban on family visits. Regarding ceasefire or negotiation status, Hamas declared commitment to the "15-point roadmap" for completing the second phase of a ceasefire agreement and urged mediators to pressure Netanyahu to abide by it. However, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly rejected the 15-point plan and reiterated that the IDF would not withdraw until Hamas is genuinely disarmed. He indicated that while discussions with the Americans are ongoing, some of their ideas are unacceptable to Israel. Netanyahu had reportedly approved a US-backed plan for a partial IDF withdrawal from three areas near Rafah last week but changed his mind in the last 24 hours.

LEBANON
Hezbollah condemned Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs for including southern Lebanon in official Israeli maps, viewing it as definitive proof of Zionist ambitions and a tactic to buy time in negotiations. Israeli forces launched artillery strikes in southern Lebanon, targeting areas in the Nabatieh governorate. Lebanese reports also indicated attacks in the villages of Al-Mansouri and Sarbin. The IDF's 55th Brigade and Yahalom forces identified and destroyed an underground pit and numerous weapons, including Kalashnikovs, anti-tank missiles, launchers, artillery, and RPGs, belonging to Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. US-brokered talks between Beirut and Tel Aviv, aimed at ending Israeli attacks and securing a phased Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory, were recently held in Rome. Switzerland is reportedly being considered as a leading candidate for a foreign monitoring force to oversee the implementation of an Israel-Lebanon agreement. Turkey has called for a meeting between Syria and Hezbollah, expressing readiness for economic and military partnership.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syrian internal security forces announced the dismantling of an ISIS terror cell in Khan-Arnabah, Quneitra Governorate, a few kilometers from the Israeli border in the Golan Heights. The cell was reportedly involved in collecting weapons and transferring explosive devices. Israeli military forces abducted a Syrian youth after a raid into a village in southern Dara'a province. Syria's Foreign Ministry announced a memorandum of understanding with Russia regarding the future of the Russian bases in Tartous and Hmeimim, outlining that Syria would take over civilian facilities, and military sites would convert into joint training centers within a three-month transition period.

In Iraq, security forces arrested a cell of three individuals directly linked to Iranian entities, who were planning attacks outside Iraq. Al-Arabiya reported the seizure of a large cache of Iranian weapons and drones from a Hashd al-Shaabi cell by the Iraqi army. Unidentified warplanes were reported in the skies of Dhi Qar governorate in southern Iraq.

GULF STATES
Yemeni Houthi forces claimed to have attacked Saudi Aramco facilities in Jizan with a drone, scoring a direct hit, in response to Saudi drone incursions into Saada and Hajjah airspace. Pro-Iranian sources also reported explosions and a fire at a gas facility in Al-Jubail, Saudi Arabia. Yemeni sources reported multiple Houthi missile and drone attacks on Mokha port in Yemen, causing fires and extensive damage, killing at least 7 and injuring 35 Saudi-backed mercenaries and Saudi officers. A ballistic missile also targeted the residence of Al-Hodeidah Governor Al-Hassan Taher in Al-Khokha, who reportedly survived. The Houthis stated these attacks targeted Saudi-backed mercenaries' positions and weapon depots.

Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan announced a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, referred to as the "Makkah Pact," describing it as similar to NATO's Article 5, with Egypt potentially joining after technical issues are resolved. This development has generated "deep strategic concerns" in Tel Aviv. An American official claimed that Saudi money was used to influence the UN Security Council's condemnation of Yemeni Armed Forces' retaliatory attacks. Oman is mediating partial negotiations between Iran and the US regarding the Strait of Hormuz. An American official claimed that approximately 8 million barrels of oil are exiting the Persian Gulf nightly via the southern corridor of the Strait of Hormuz with US military coordination, and the US intends to increase this flow until a deal is reached with Iran.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Iran's Uncompromising Stance on Strait of Hormuz**: Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Secretary Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr and IRGC Spokesperson Mohebbi stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US accepts six broad conditions, including ending all threats and hostilities against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Gaza, Yemen, and Iraq, lifting the naval blockade, withdrawing US forces, providing full war reparations, lifting all sanctions, and releasing frozen assets. This complicates US efforts for reopening and de-escalation.
2.  **Significant Leadership Appointments in Iran**: Major General Mohsen Rezaei was appointed as the Leader's representative to the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) and subsequently as SNSC Secretary by President Pezeshkian, replacing Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr, who was appointed as the Leader's political adviser.
3.  **Netanyahu Rejects Gaza Peace Roadmap**: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly rejected the "Gaza Board of Peace 15-point plan" and reiterated that the IDF would not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas is genuinely disarmed, asserting his commitment to prevent the formation of a Palestinian state while he is in office.
4.  **Intensified Houthi Attacks in Yemen and Saudi Arabia**: Yemeni Houthi forces launched multiple missile and drone attacks, including a direct hit on an Aramco refinery in Jizan, Saudi Arabia, and a fourth wave of assaults on Mokha port in Yemen. These attacks resulted in at least 7 killed and 35 injured among Saudi-backed mercenaries and Saudi officers, and a ballistic missile targeted the Al-Hodeidah Governor's residence.
5.  **US Military Munitions Shortages and Drone Crash**: The Pentagon ordered military contractors to accelerate weapon production to address critical munitions shortages caused by the "Iran war." Additionally, a US MQ-9 drone crashed near Chabelley Airfield in Djibouti after reporting distress, with some Yemeni sources claiming it was shot down in Bab al-Mandab.
6.  **Emergence of Makkah Defense Pact**: Turkey's Foreign Minister announced a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, dubbed the "Makkah Pact," potentially including Egypt, which is generating "deep strategic concerns" in Tel Aviv.
7.  **Israeli Operations Against Hezbollah in Southern Lebanon**: IDF's 55th Brigade and Yahalom forces successfully located and destroyed an underground pit used for Hezbollah weapon storage and seized numerous weapons in southern Lebanon. Israeli artillery strikes were also reported in the Nabatieh governorate.
8.  **Syria-Russia Agreement on Military Bases**: Syria and Russia signed a Memorandum of Understanding regarding the future of Russian military bases in Tartous and Hmeimim, with Syria assuming control of civilian facilities and military sites transitioning to joint training centers within three months.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are significantly high. Iran's firm, expanded conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz create a direct confrontation with US policy and risk military intervention, especially given the ongoing US naval blockade and US consideration of renewed military action. Netanyahu's categorical rejection of the Gaza peace plan and a Palestinian state ensures continued conflict in the Palestinian territories. The ongoing Houthi attacks on Saudi and Yemeni government targets represent an active flashpoint with high casualty counts, risking broader regional instability. The US military is actively accelerating weapon production, indicating preparations for sustained conflict in the region, while a US MQ-9 drone crash under unclear circumstances in Djibouti adds to the volatile operational environment. Residents in western Tehran reported hearing loud fighter jet sounds, suggesting heightened aerial activity or military exercises, further underscoring an active flashpoint. Military posture changes include Iran's Army Ground Force on "full combat readiness," warning against invasions, and the US maintaining its naval blockade while seeking to increase oil flow out of the Persian Gulf. Red lines are hardening, with Iran's demands for reparations and a cessation of hostilities unlikely to be met by the US, and Israel's non-negotiable stance on Hamas's disarmament and a Palestinian state.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** is maintaining a "low key" approach to Iran, focusing on economic pressure and the naval blockade, while Trump is reportedly considering declaring victory without a nuclear deal if the Strait of Hormuz reopens. However, the Pentagon is actively pushing military contractors to accelerate weapon production due to shortages from the "Iran war," and US officials informed Israel that the US wants an end to conflicts on three active fronts.
**Gulf states** are actively engaged, with Saudi Arabia being a direct target of Houthi attacks. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have formed a new "Makkah Pact" defense alliance, which may include Egypt, creating "deep strategic concerns" for Israel. Oman is mediating partial talks between Iran and the US regarding maritime routes in the Strait of Hormuz.
**Egypt's** Foreign Minister emphasized the necessity of a complete Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and is considering joining the Makkah Pact.
**Russia** has reached a memorandum of understanding with Syria on the future of military bases in Tartous and Hmeimim. Russia's Rosatom plans to increase its staff at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant to 100 by autumn, contingent on no further escalation between Iran and the US.
**China** and Russia are reported by the New York Times to benefit from the US's depleted munitions stockpiles due to the Iran war.
**Turkey** is a key player in the new Makkah Pact and is reportedly calling for a meeting between Syria and Hezbollah, offering economic and military partnership.
**Hamas** declared its commitment to the "15-point roadmap" for a ceasefire in Gaza and urged mediators to pressure Israel into compliance.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions were noted in the reporting of Mohsen Rezaei's appointment as SNSC Secretary, with several Iranian news agencies initially publishing and then deleting the news before re-releasing it, possibly indicating internal power struggles or messaging control issues. Trump's statements about "low keying it" with Iran and not rushing decisions appear to contradict earlier reports of his readiness for widespread military action, potentially a calculated diplomatic posture. There is an uncorroborated report from Shargh about a fire at Al-Jubail gas facility in Saudi Arabia, which was not confirmed by Houthi claims or other sources. Houthi claims of hitting a US MQ-9 drone in Bab al-Mandab are unverified and contradict US embassy reports of a distress call and crash near Chabelley Airfield without specifying a hostile hit.

Unverified claims include the "Day of Wrath" in Thessaloniki, Greece, reports of Netanyahu learning of his own change of mind regarding Rafah troop withdrawal via media, and speculative claims about Mujtaba Khamenei's public appearances and the use of AI/Photoshop for his images, suggesting internal rumor-mongering or disinformation.

Propaganda indicators are evident across sources: Iranian and Houthi media consistently frame their actions as "resistance" against "US-Israeli aggression" and portray the US as seeking to dominate. Israeli sources emphasize IDF successes and Netanyahu's unwavering stance against Hamas and Iran, often highlighting the "failures" of the enemy. The use of highly charged language (e.g., "Allah Akbar" by NAYA, "cut off feet" by Iranian military) serves to rally domestic support and project strength.

Reporting gaps include a lack of independent verification for most battlefield claims from all sides. Specific details of the "Gaza Board of Peace 15-point plan" and the "Islamabad MoU" are not fully provided, hindering a complete understanding of the negotiating positions. Furthermore, comprehensive information on the "Makkah Pact" (beyond Turkey's Foreign Minister's statements) and its exact implications for regional security is scarce. There is also a lack of specific details on ongoing "Iran war" activities, focusing more on US logistical and economic impacts rather than direct combat.
